full_judgment:
19. The learned Deputy Attorney General submits that the application suffers from non-joinder of necessary party whose presence is essential for the disposal of the rule. In this connection he relied on the case of Joinal Abedin Vs. The Collector of Central Excise and Land Customs (West Zone), Chittagong reported in 1959 PLD, Dacca 342. In the said case the petition was directed against the Collector of Central Excise and Land Customs (W. Zone) Chittagong who had merely carried out the orders of the Central Board of Revenue. The Board was not made a party in the Writ petition. The Writ was issued against the Collector alone. It was held that the writ issued will not be effective because the Collector will not be in a position to carry out the mandate of the court. Mandamus will not go when it appears that it would be futile in its result. In the instant case writ has been issued against the Govt. of Bangladesh who has not denied that on 1.7.80 Towab was not allowed to re-enter Bangladesh by some of its officers. In the facts of the instant case the writ asked for and issued would not be futile in the absence of the officers of the Govt. of Bangladesh who refused Towab's re-entry into Bangladesh. 

 31. Mr. Mainul Husein submits that under Article 11 no one is empowered to reuse entry to a Bangladesh citizen into Bangladesh holding prima facie a valid passport. If non-compliance of rule 9(1) of the Passport Rules 1974 be regarded as an offence, then the offender could be punished with imprisonment for a term not exceeding 3 months or with fine not exceeding Tk. 500/- or with both for such an offence. The holder of the passport could not be refused entry into Bangladesh under the law. Mr. Hosein submits that if there has been any contravention of Passport Act or Rules then Towab could be prosecuted in accordance with law and/or his passport could be impounded. He further submits that no case has yet been filed against Towab for contravention of any law.
